newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa makes pay counter-offer to unions.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa makes pay counter-offer to unions.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG made a counter-offer to unions on Wednesday in pay talks for the group's 50,000 employees, the public sector union OeTV said.

The proposal involved a one-off payment for the remainder of 1996 and for 1997, followed by a percentage pay rise in 1998. The offer also included participation in a profit-sharing scheme, an OeTV spokesman told Reuters.
The agreement proposed by the airline would run until the end of 1998.
The union said it would discuss the airline's proposals. The spokesman did not give details of how much would be paid out in the percentage pay rise for 1998.
A spokesman for the other union involved in the pay talks, the white collar DAG union, was unavailable for comment.
A Lufthansa spokeswoman declined to comment on the current state of play in the pay negotiations.
OeTV had earlier demanded a 2.3 percent wage rise while DAG was looking for a four percent increase.
